sentences.text: Has anyone verified the axle spread on car eighty-eight, or are we just trusting the stencil? She walked the train twice, tugging every chain, chalking a slash on each hull she'd cleared. "Watch your overhang!" the ground guide yelled, palms up, as the driver eased the armored hull across the span plates. Sixteen flatcars, nine hours of daylight, one working overhead crane — you do the math, sergeant. A gust snatched the tarp off car twelve, and three soldiers chased the flapping canvas down the ballast like it owed them money. Rain hammered the tarps all night, and by dawn every manifest in the clerk's binder had gone soft at the edges. "Chain it at four corners or it walks off the flatcar at the first grade crossing — simple as that." By 0500 the loading ramp was slick with frost, so the ground guides shortened every signal and doubled every pause. The dispatcher's voice crackled over the radio: "Your window closes at fourteen hundred, loaded or not." Grease-pencil numbers on the glacis matched the manifest, but the serial plates told a different story. Forklifts shuttled crates of spare track pads between warehouses while the crane crew argued over the lift plan. We lost forty minutes hunting for shackles that turned out to be buried under a tarp in the third conex. All tracked vehicles must be secured with grade-eighty chain assemblies inspected within the preceding ninety days, per the movement order. Nobody tells you in school that half of military logistics is arguing with a railroad clerk about tarp dimensions. When the protein skimmer hums off-key, Mr. Okafor hears it from the kitchen and comes out wiping his hands. Honestly? Half our Yelp photos are of the aquarium, not the food. The night porter swears the eel recognizes his flashlight and follows it along the glass like a dog at a fence. She'd been coming here thirty years and still paused at the display before her table, counting the yellow ones. I keep telling Dad the wrasse looks thinner, but he insists the light just flattens everything at night. Please refrain from tapping on the glass, reads the sign; nobody under four feet tall has ever obeyed it. What is the meaning of the word tank?
